description:
## What

Codify the architectural principle decided 2026-05-13 (Mark) as a new
non-negotiable in `AGENTS.md`, sibling to non-negotiable #5
(framework-not-policy three-mode architecture).

## The principle

The workspace's fast in-process `Profile`/`Lint` types ship the current
rules from the latest BR snapshot. Historical-regime replay and
caller-pinned spec versions go out-of-process to `pkix-policy-zlint`.

Worth a separate non-negotiable because it cuts on a different axis from
non-negotiable #5:

- **Non-negotiable #5** governs **who owns the policy specification**:
  standards-body (workspace authors) / industry-forum (sibling adapter
  crate) / site-local (consumer).
- **This new non-negotiable** governs **when the policy is evaluated**:
  current regime (workspace) / historical or version-pinned (external
  validator).

A rule that the spec ITSELF writes as time-keyed (SC-081 phased validity
cap, `sc081_validity_cap(not_before_unix)`) stays in-process because the
time-keying is part of the current rule's definition — it's transcribing
what the spec literally says, not maintaining a delta history.

## Draft text

Add as a new non-negotiable (#6 or appropriately numbered) under
"Non-negotiable constraints" in `AGENTS.md`:

```
6. **Current-regime only; historical and version-pinned postures go out-of-process.**

   Workspace `Profile` and `Lint` types snapshot the current rules from
   the latest BR text. They evaluate "is this cert conforming under
   today's rules?" — including rules the spec itself writes as
   time-keyed (SC-081 phased validity cap, future similar). The
   time-keying is part of the current rule's definition, not historical
   replay.

   The workspace does NOT ship validators that evaluate against:
   - rules in force at a past time, with predicates that have since
     been changed or removed (historical-regime replay), or
   - a caller-pinned spec version (version-frozen replay).

   For either posture, use `pkix-policy-zlint` with a version-pinned
   lint set. zlint owns the historian role for vendor policy.

   `ValidationPolicy::new(now_unix)` selects the moment at which
   validity-period checks are evaluated, NOT the moment whose rules are
   in force. This is documented on the API (see PKIX-* bead for the
   rustdoc clarification).
```

(Cross-reference the sibling beads in the parenthetical once they are
filed.)

## Why this matters

Without codification, future agents and future-Mark will repeatedly
relitigate "should pkix-profiles-cabf take a version parameter?" /
"should the workspace ship historical replay?" The 2026-05-13 chat
arrived at the answer; this bead writes it down so subsequent sessions
inherit the decision.

It also clarifies an existing ambiguity in `ValidationPolicy::new(now_unix)`:
callers may intuit that passing an older `now_unix` gives them "rules in
force at that older time." It doesn't. Documenting the semantic on the
API surfaces the trap before users walk into it.

## Acceptance

- AGENTS.md amended with the non-negotiable text above (final numbering
  per where it slots in).
- `CHANGELOG.md` workspace-root entry under `[unreleased]` documenting
  the amendment.
- Commit message: `docs(AGENTS.md): codify temporal-posture
  non-negotiable (current-regime in-process; historical out-of-process)`.

## Cross-references

- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5 (sibling architectural principle; framework/policy axis)
- AGENTS.md "Project phase and decision framing" (prelaunch framing)
- PKIX-mzsk (spec-taxonomy principle; sibling principle on the
  taxonomy-depth axis)
- PKIX-jy95 (`pkix-policy-zlint` — where historical-regime replay lives)
- 2026-05-13 chat record (decision rationale; framing originated when
  Mark proposed "if its not currentnow, it has to run thru long path
  that ends with the external validator")

## Not in scope

- Implementing the phased-rule helper catalog (filed as sibling bead).
- The `now_unix` rustdoc clarification (filed as sibling bead).
- The PKIX-jbvb.8 multi-generation Profile types question (different
  axis: taxonomy depth, not temporal posture).
title: AGENTS.md: codify temporal-posture non-negotiable (current-regime only; historical/version-pinned out-of-process)
